name: Unde Kaili
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: No description of Unde Kaili found; Kaili literature (e.g. Esser, Pusat Bahasa) targets Ledo, not Unde; sulang.org unreachable.

sources.citation: Sulawesi Language Alliance (David Mead). 2014. 'Kaili, Unde' language page and resource indexes (grammar descriptions, phonology and orthography descriptions, word lists, survey reports), sulang.org
sources.note: No resource of any kind listed for Kaili Unde (Documentation tab 'not yet functional'); the only Kaili items on the whole site are Mead 2014, the Esser 1934 Ledo scan and a Kruyt 1937 text. Live site refuses connections; read via the Internet Archive (2024).
Nothing; names Banava/Banawa, dialects Lole (negator unde) and Ganti (negator ndepuu), 25,000 speakers (2007 SIL); no bibliography.

sources.citation: Mead, David. 2014 [v1 2010]. How do you slice the pie? Ways of looking at the Kaili language area of Central Sulawesi, Indonesia. Sulang Language Data and Working Papers: Survey Reports 1. Sulawesi Language Alliance, 24 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Armchair classification survey (Adriani 1898 to Ethnologue 2009); establishes Unde = Loli/Lole, Ndepuu = Ganti, Barr & Barr 1979 'Banava' = Unde + Ndepuu; reference list read for Unde-relevant works (none descriptive).

sources.citation: Triana, Nening. [undated, c.2013-2015]. Struktur frase endosentris bahasa Kaili dialek Unde. Jurnal Bahasa dan Sastra (Prodi Pendidikan Bahasa Indonesia, FKIP Universitas Tadulako), 13 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Syntax-only student article on Unde endocentric phrases (data from Banawa, Donggala); no phonology section; a full-text search for stress/accent tekanan/fonologi/aksen/suku kata = 0 hits.

sources.citation: Nur, Yunidar. 2011. Saling pengertian antar dialek bahasa Kaili di Lembah Palu. LiNGUA: Jurnal Ilmu Bahasa dan Sastra 5(2). doi:10.18860/ling.v5i2.621, 7 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic mutual-intelligibility test among Ledo, Da'a, Unde (Loli Tasiburi, Banawa district) and Rai speakers; no phonological description.

sources.citation: Esser, S. J. 1934. Handleiding voor de beoefening der Ledo-taal: Inleiding (pp. 1-25). Bandoeng: Nix. (sulang.org scan, Dutch original, scanned here)
sources.note: §I.4 p.5: 'De klemtoon valt in het L. steeds op de voorlaatste lettergreep, en verschuift bij de aanhechting van achtervoegsels of eenlettergrepige partikels' (footnote 3: this state is borrowed from Buginese, traces of older accentuation remain). Explicitly about 'het L.' = Ledo (ledo1238); the introduction names Ledo as the chief of the 'Kailische dialecten' but says nothing about stress in Banawa/Unde.

sources.citation: Adriani, N. & Alb. C. Kruyt. 1912. De Bare'e-sprekende Toradja's van Midden-Celebes, vols 1-2 (Internet Archive microform scanned)
sources.note: Nothing on Kaili Unde (ethnographic volumes; a full-text search for stress/accent Banawa/Loli/Ganti/klemtoon finds only Pamona word notes). Part 3 (1914, language overview) is not on the Internet Archive.

sources.citation: Rahim, Abdillah A., H. Hasan Basri & Ali Efendy. 1998. Tata bahasa Kaili. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa. xiii+101 pp.

sources.note: Pusat Bahasa grammar sketches normally open with a fonologi section including tekanan; must check which Kaili variety (Ledo vs Unde/Banawa) it describes; the Kemdikbud repository (repositori.kemendikdasmen.go.

sources.citation: Martens, Michael P. 1990. Proto Kaili-Pamona (Volume 3 of the research results of the Uma language field program in Central Sulawesi). SIL draft manuscript, 221 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 92394.

sources.note: Comparative-historical study; the only work in OLAC for unz besides Ethnologue/Glottolog; subject languages include Unde Kaili; ch. 4 'Summary of grammatical features of Kaili-Pamona languages' and ch. 3 on phoneme reflexes are the likeliest places for a per-language or subgroup stress statement.
